meta.name: Inference for Means (7.1-7.9)
meta.subject: AP Statistics
meta.description: AP Statistics Unit 7 practice for Topics 7.1-7.9: Introducing Statistics: Should I Worry About Error? (7.1), Constructing a Confidence Interval for a Population Mean (7.2), Justifying a Claim About a Population Mean Based on a Confidence Interval (7.3), Setting Up a Test for a Population Mean (7.4), Carrying Out a Test for a Population Mean (7.5), Confidence Intervals for the Difference of Two Means (7.6), Justifying a Claim About the Difference of Two Means Based on a Confidence Interval (7.7), Setting Up a Test for the Difference of Two Population Means (7.8), and Carrying Out and Interpreting a Test for the Difference of Two Population Means (7.9). Includes one-sample t-intervals, significance tests for a population mean, and two-sample inference for the difference of two means.

perField.procedureAnswer: Use this checklist: one sample, quantitative data, and estimating a mean mu. That points to a one-sample t-interval.
perField.conditionsMet: All three must work: random sample, 10% condition when sampling without replacement, and n >= 30 or no strong skewness/outliers if n < 30.
perField.conditionsExplain: Mention the random condition, the 10% check, and either n >= 30 or the sample-shape check for skewness and outliers.
perField.tStarAnswer: For a confidence interval for a mean, use a t critical value with df = n - 1, not a z critical value.
perField.meAnswer: Margin of error = t* x s / sqrt(n). Use the sample standard deviation s and divide by the square root of n.
perField.ciLower: First compute the margin of error, then subtract it from x-bar to get the lower bound.
perField.ciUpper: First compute the margin of error, then add it to x-bar to get the upper bound.
perField.evidenceAnswer: The evidence is the observed difference in the sample means, not the null value of 0 and not one sample mean by itself.
perField.nullDiffAnswer: If the treatment makes no difference, the difference in sample means should be centered at 0.
perField.chanceExplainAnswer: Chance-variation explanation = no real treatment effect, and the observed difference came from random assignment alone.
perField.simProbAnswer: Estimate the probability with tail count divided by total simulations, then write the answer as a decimal.
perField.conclusionAnswer: If the simulated probability is small, rule out chance variation as a likely explanation. If it is not small, chance variation is still plausible.
perField.intervalInterpretAnswer: Use the template: We are C% confident that the interval from lower to upper captures the population mean in context.
perField.claimJustifyAnswer: If the claimed value is inside the interval, it is plausible. If every value in the interval is above or below the benchmark, that supports a one-sided claim.
perField.confidenceLevelAnswer: Interpret confidence level with repeated random sampling: about C% of intervals from many samples would capture the population mean.
perField.sampleSizeEffectAnswer: For a mean interval, margin of error is proportional to 1 / sqrt(n). Quadrupling n cuts the margin of error about in half.
perField.confidenceLevelEffectAnswer: Keeping everything else the same, a lower confidence level uses a smaller critical value and gives a smaller margin of error.
perField.nullHypothesisAnswer: The null hypothesis uses an equality and the population parameter mu. Do not use x-bar in the null hypothesis.
perField.alternativeHypothesisAnswer: The alternative hypothesis uses a strict inequality. Choose <, >, or not equal based on the question of interest.
perField.parameterDefinitionAnswer: Define mu as the population mean in context, not the sample mean and not one individual value.
perField.testProcedureAnswer: This is a significance test about one population mean, so the procedure is a one-sample t-test for a population mean.
perField.testConditionsMet: Check for a random sample or randomized experiment, the 10% condition when sampling without replacement, and n >= 30 or no strong skewness/outliers if n < 30.
perField.testConditionsExplain: Mention the random condition, the 10% check, and either n >= 30 or the sample-shape check for skewness and outliers.
perField.testStatisticAnswer: Use t = (sample statistic - null value) / (s / sqrt(n)). For paired data, use the sample mean of the differences and the standard deviation of the differences.
perField.pValueRegionAnswer: Match the tail area to the alternative hypothesis: > means right tail, < means left tail, and not equal means both tails.
perField.pValueAnswer: Use the test statistic and the alternative together. A two-sided test doubles the one-tail probability.
perField.pValueInterpretAnswer: Start with 'Assuming the null hypothesis is true...' Then describe the chance of getting a sample result this extreme or more extreme by random chance alone.
perField.testConclusionAnswer: Compare the p-value to alpha. If p <= alpha, reject H0 and support the alternative. If p > alpha, fail to reject H0.
perField.diffMeansProcedureAnswer: Two groups, quantitative data, and estimating mu1 - mu2 with an interval point to a two-sample t-interval.
perField.diffMeansConditionsMet: Check for two independent random samples or random assignment, the 10% condition when sampling without replacement, and whether both sample sizes are at least 30 or both sample distributions show no strong skewness or outliers.
perField.diffMeansConditionsExplain: Mention independence, the 10% condition when it applies, and that both samples must be large enough or both sample distributions must be roughly normal with no extreme skewness or outliers.
perField.diffMeansMeAnswer: For a two-sample t-interval, margin of error = t* x sqrt((s1^2 / n1) + (s2^2 / n2)).
perField.diffMeansCiLower: First find x-bar1 - x-bar2 and the margin of error, then subtract the margin of error for the lower bound.
perField.diffMeansCiUpper: First find x-bar1 - x-bar2 and the margin of error, then add the margin of error for the upper bound.
perField.diffMeansIntervalInterpretAnswer: Interpret the interval for the population difference in means in the stated order, such as female minus male, not for individual observations.
perField.diffMeansZeroValueAnswer: If the two population means are equal, then group 1 minus group 2 is 0. That is the no-difference benchmark.
perField.diffMeansZeroPlausibleAnswer: Check whether 0 is inside the confidence interval. Inside means no difference is plausible; outside means 0 is not plausible.
perField.diffMeansClaimJustifyAnswer: Use 0 as the benchmark for no difference. If 0 is outside the interval, that supports a directional claim; if 0 is inside, the claim is not supported.
perField.diffMeansClaimConclusionAnswer: State the conclusion cautiously in context. Do not say the claim is proved, and do not say someone is wrong just because 0 is in the interval.
perField.diffMeansConfidenceLevelAnswer: Interpret confidence level with repeated random sampling: about C% of intervals from many sample pairs would capture the population difference in means.
perField.diffMeansNullHypothesisAnswer: For a test about two means, the null says no difference: use the population means and set group 1 minus group 2 equal to 0.
perField.diffMeansAlternativeHypothesisAnswer: The alternative uses a strict inequality and the population means. Match the direction to the claim in context.
perField.diffMeansAlternativeTypeAnswer: Directional claims use a one-sided alternative. Claims that say the means are different use a two-sided alternative.
perField.diffMeansReverseOrderAnswer: If you reverse the subtraction order in a one-sided hypothesis, you must reverse the inequality too.
perField.diffMeansParameterDefinitionAnswer: Define each parameter as a population mean for its group, not a sample mean, not one individual value, and not a total.
perField.diffMeansTestStatisticAnswer: Use t = ((x-bar1 - x-bar2) - 0) / sqrt((s1^2 / n1) + (s2^2 / n2)). Under H0, the null value for the difference is 0.
perField.diffMeansPValueRegionAnswer: Match the tail area to the alternative hypothesis for the difference in means: > means right tail, < means left tail, and not equal means both tails.
perField.diffMeansPValueAnswer: Use the test statistic and the alternative together. For a two-sample test, a two-sided alternative doubles the one-tail probability.
perField.diffMeansPValueInterpretAnswer: Start with 'Assuming the null hypothesis is true...' Then describe the chance of getting a difference in sample means this extreme or more extreme by random chance alone.
perField.diffMeansTestConclusionAnswer: Compare the p-value to alpha. If p <= alpha, reject H0 and support the alternative. If p > alpha, fail to reject H0.
perField.diffMeansComparePValueAlphaAnswer: Compare the two numbers directly. If the p-value is at or below alpha, it goes in the reject-H0 branch; if it is larger, it goes in the fail-to-reject branch.
perField.diffMeansTestDecisionAnswer: The formal decision is about H0: reject H0 when p <= alpha; otherwise fail to reject H0. Do not say accept H0.
perField.diffMeansStatSigAnswer: Statistically significant means the p-value is at or below alpha. If p > alpha, the result is not statistically significant at that level.
perField.diffMeansEvidenceAnswer: Translate the decision into evidence language: reject H0 means convincing statistical evidence for the alternative; fail to reject H0 means not convincing statistical evidence. Do not say prove.
